paras: The threatened lynching of Isaac Ford took place in July 1903 in Grayson County, Texas, after Ford, a young Black man, was arrested near Sherman and charged with criminal assault on a seven-year-old girl. Officers moved him in secret to the Fort Worth jail, and on July 23 he hanged himself there. The Associated Press reported that mob violence had been threatened, and papers outside Texas headlined the death as a suicide to avoid lynching.

According to a Denison dispatch, Lillian Moreland, the daughter of a Sherman man, was assaulted at Sherman on Sunday, July 12. A Sherman dispatch in the same paper gave her name as Lillian Moran, and one Bryan Morning Eagle item put the offense at Dorchester and the girl's age at eight.

Sheriff Russell of Grayson County and Deputy Sheriff Wise of Bonham arrested Ford on the night of July 20, held him overnight at Denison, and sent him to Fort Worth with Deputy Sheriff Duer the next morning. The San Antonio Daily Light reported that he made a full confession, that the arrest was kept secret until he was gone, and that 'considerable excitement' prevailed at Sherman.

In an interview at Fort Worth, Ford denied the charge and said he could prove an alibi. He said that on his way to work at a thresher he met four men, two white and two Black, who accused him and said they would kill him unless he admitted it. By his account one of the white men struck him on the head, cutting a gash over his right eye, and he confessed out of fear; the reporter noted the wound.

After hearing the charges read from a paper, Ford spent Wednesday night tearing a blanket into a rope in view of other prisoners, according to the Bryan Morning Eagle. At about 11 o'clock on Thursday, July 23, he tied the rope to the grating of his cell, stood on a bucket and kicked it away, and was found dead.
No report of an inquest, of any arrest of the men Ford accused, or of action against those who threatened him appears in the coverage found.

The Associated Press sent a two-sentence item from Fort Worth ending 'Mob violence was threatened.' The Richmond Times Dispatch headed it 'Negro Killed Himself to Avoid Lynching' and the Savannah Morning News 'Negro Hanged Himself to Escape a Mob,' while the Raleigh News and Observer and the Newberry Herald and News ran it among news briefs. A Dallas News special, carried by the Birmingham Age-Herald, the Montgomery Advertiser and the Atlanta Constitution, reported the blanket rope but no mob.

Texas papers carried more detail. The San Antonio Daily Light headed the arrest 'Arrested for Rape' and 'a Negro's Crime,' yet two days later printed Ford's account of a confession forced by threats and a blow at length. The Bryan Morning Eagle ran his denial as 'Says He Is Innocent' and his death as 'Suicides in Jail.' No coverage in the Black press was found.

The arresting side reported that Ford made a full confession, while Ford said it was extracted by four men who struck him and threatened his life. Most reports placed the alleged assault at Sherman, but one placed it at Dorchester.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Isaac Ford
bases: A threatened lynching: the AP wire reported that mob violence was threatened against Ford after his arrest and Texas specials described excitement at Sherman and his secret removal to Fort Worth (A5, A1); he died by his own hand in jail, not at the hands of a mob (A2, A3).

Ford hanged himself in the Fort Worth jail (A2, A3, A5); no mob reached him, so no one was killed by a group, though a mob was reported threatening him over the assault charge (A5) and he said four men threatened to kill him unless he confessed (A2).

The arrest, the charge and the jail suicide are reported independently by the AP wire (A5), the Dallas News special (A7), San Antonio Daily Light specials (A1, A2) and the Bryan Morning Eagle (A3); the mob threat itself rests on the AP line (A5) and the Light's report of excitement and a secret removal (A1).

accounts.label: Officers' and Sherman dispatches
accounts.gist: A negro was arrested near Sherman and made a full confession; the arrest was kept secret and he was taken to Fort Worth before Sherman people knew, amid considerable excitement.

accounts.label: Ford's own statement
accounts.gist: On his way to work at a thresher he was met by four men, two white and two Black, who accused him, struck him on the head and threatened to kill him until he said he did it; he said he could prove an alibi.

accounts.label: AP wire
accounts.gist: Ford, accused of criminal assault on a little girl in Grayson County, hanged himself in jail; mob violence was threatened.

accounts.label: Jail account (Fort Worth)
accounts.gist: Ford spent Wednesday night making a rope from a blanket in view of other prisoners, prayed Thursday morning, and hanged himself from the cell grating at 11 o'clock after hearing the charges read from a paper.

framing.detail: AP copy ran under headlines linking the suicide to the mob: 'Negro Killed Himself to Avoid Lynching' and 'Negro Hanged Himself to Escape a Mob.'
The Dallas News special, carried in Birmingham, Montgomery and Atlanta, reported only the suicide and the blanket rope under 'Negro Hangs Himself.'

The San Antonio Daily Light headed the arrest 'Arrested for Rape' and 'a Negro's Crime' and called him the alleged assailant, but printed his denial and his account of a beaten-out confession at length.
The Bryan Morning Eagle ran the suicide as 'Suicides in Jail' and Ford's denial as 'Says He Is Innocent.'

conflicts.note: Most reports, including the Sherman and Denison dispatches, say Sherman; one Bryan item says Dorchester.
The Denison dispatch and later reports say Moreland; the Sherman dispatch in the same issue says Moran.
